title: QBR Catalyst Kit: Upgrade Warm-Paths (Dedicated -> Private, SLA Add-ons)
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a lightweight QBR ‘catalyst kit’ for reps and CSMs to run account conversations that nudge healthy dedicated customers toward Dedicated->Private migrations or premium SLA add-ons. Focus is on warm-paths (accounts already showing scale, compliance asks, or reliability concerns).

Quick note to self:
- This is intentionally tactical: modular agenda blocks, metric callouts, and a compact renewal/commitment tracker.
- Keep experiments small: A/B different offer bundles and measure commit-to-conversion within 90 days.

QBR agenda (30–45m recommended; choose blocks):
1) 5m — Check-in + wins since last QBR (customer voice + Redwood wins)
   - Customer highlights (features adopted, latency improvements)
   - Any open escalations or compliance gaps
2) 8m — Usage & economics snapshot (visualize delta vs baseline)
   - Tokens/day, peak RPS, tail-latency p95, cache hit rate, unit-cost/1000 tokens
   - Cost-per-feature tradeoffs (batching, quantization)
3) 10m — Risk & opportunity signal map (explicit callouts)
   - Risk flags: sustained 10%+ tail increase, multi-region needs, data residency ask
   - Opportunity signals: consistent >=3% weekly growth in request volume, repeated capacity throttles, exec/Security outreach
4) 10m — Proposal block (choose 1–2 recommended paths)
   - Path A: Premium SLA add-on (4-hour incident response, 99.95% uptime) — small uplift, quick contract amendment
   - Path B: Dedicated -> Private migration pilot (VPC + customer-managed KMS) — 90-day pilot, success metrics: <10ms added network overhead, zero data egress incidents
   - Path C: Capacity commitment top-up (reserved slots) + cost smoothing; include predictable burst buffer
5) 5m — Next steps, owners, timeline, and commitment signal checklist

Suggested metrics to include on the QBR slide pack (one-line description each):
- Avg tokens/day (30d / 90d), growth rate
- Peak concurrent streams and 95th percentile latency
- Cache hit rate and evictions (shows opportunity for prefix caching)
- Monthly unit cost (hosted) vs projected private TCO (3-year window)
- Incident frequency and mean-time-to-recovery (MTTR)
- Product-led adoption signals (SDK integrations, function-calls usage)

Renewal & commitment tracker (compact table — copy to sheet for live use):
Columns: Account | Renewal window | Current SKU | Proposed path | Estimated uplift ($/mo) | Tech owner | Exec sponsor | Commitment signal | Next touch | Status
Example row (text):
- AcmeRetail | 2026-08-31 | Dedicated-M | Private-pilot | $18,000/mo (projected) | Tom B. | VP Eng (Acme) | Completed infra checklist, security POC scheduled | 2026-03-30 | negotiation

Outbound cadence for warm-path customers (playable sequence):
- Day 0 (post-QBR): Send tailored follow-up email with 1) executive summary, 2) proposed path slide, 3) 3 success metrics to track during pilot.
- Day 7: Technical sync invite (30m) to scope migration pilot or SLA terms. Attach migration checklist.
- Day 21: Internal readiness check; if stalled, engage Solutions Eng and schedule an exec drop-in.
- Day 45: Formal pilot kickoff or signed amendment. If no commitment, run a consolidation analysis to propose lower-risk offers (e.g., regional private node).

Technical validation checklist (for Private migration pilots):
- Authentication and KMS integration plan validated
- VPC peering/PrivateLink requirements captured and tested in staging
- Baseline performance runbook created (p95, p99, throughput)
- Data governance and audit logging acceptance from customer security
- Rollback plan: clear fallbacks to shared/dedicated endpoint with routing TTLs

Pricing & sample offers (examples to adapt; attach legal-approved language in final doc):
- SLA Add-on: +10–18% ARR uplift depending on tier; includes 4-hour response, monthly incident review, prioritized capacity.
- Private Pilot: Free 30-day pilot with success metrics; conversion discounts tiered by committed GPUs/throughput.
- Capacity Top-Up: 6- or 12-month reserved slot contracts with auto-scale credits for first 30 days.

Objection playbook (short responses):
- "Too expensive" -> show delta: predicted per-token TCO vs current + value of reduced latency/support overhead. Offer 60-day price-protection if pilot converts.
- "Not enough SLAs" -> map specific incidents to SLA clauses and propose a tailored incident runbook + quarterly reviews.
- "Security concerns" -> run the KMS/PE/Logging checklist and offer an executive session with Security & Solutions Eng.

Signals that justify escalation to Sales Engineering / Solutions Eng: (automate triage via tags in CRM)
- >3 unplanned production outages in 90 days
- Sustained request-volume growth >25% q/q with regular throttling
- Compliance/regulatory milestone that requires isolation (e.g., PCI/PHI jurisdictional hold)

Open questions / experiments to run (tracking hypotheses):
- Hypothesis A: A 3-month private pilot with an acceptance gate at 45 days increases conversion by 2x vs immediate PO request.
- Hypothesis B: Bundling a 99.95% SLA with a 6-month reserved slot reduces churn by 15% for top-10 accounts.
- Experiment note: Randomize price-protection windows (30d vs 60d) across pilot offers and track conversion velocity.

Template email: (short version for follow up)
Subject: Thanks — QBR recap & next steps (Private pilot proposal)
Hi <Name>,
Thanks again for a productive QBR. Attached is a short summary and a proposed 90-day Private pilot that targets your data-residency and reliability asks. If you’re open, let’s lock a 30-minute technical kickoff next week to scope KMS and networking.
Regards,
Aisha (CS)

Appendix: quick checklist for CSM before the QBR
- Pull 90d usage and highlight 3 trends (growth, cost spikes, error patterns)
- Run the 'latency vs cost' micro-sim to show private TCO delta
- Seed the QBR with a proposed path (A/B) and internal ask: which SE and which legal template to use

Notes and formatting guidance for slide pack:
- Keep 1 slide per agenda block; use 1:1 charts for cost vs latency; add a single table for the renewal tracker snapshot.
- Include a 2-line TL;DR for execs with clear ask: (1) what we want them to approve, (2) ideal timeline, (3) owner.

Last thoughts:
This kit is intentionally compact — run it, capture outcomes in the renewal tracker sheet, and iterate. Aim for 3 pilots per quarter and bake learnings into pricing.
